THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE  75

Y. M. C. A.

It is designed to have a Young Men's Christian Association for the purpose of wielding a good influence among the boys.

The Y.M.C.A. did exist in almost all colleges, and the results have been many and good, affecting social and moral improvement. Nothing will be more uplifting to a young man than to throw him with active Christians, Methodists, Presbyterians, and all other religious denominations may meet here as brothers.

In addition to thus encouraging the students' voluntary participation in their own evangelical activities, the College further carried out the idea by having daily chapel exercises with compulsory attendance. Excuses were given for missing chapel, and if too many were received the delinquent student stood in danger of corporal punishment. These exercises began the day's work. At the top of the bell the whole student body gathered—women in the upper gallery (the large room in the original Abernathy building, which could be partitioned into two sections and later used as a classroom) and boys on the ground floor, for an exercise consisting of Bible reading, without comment, and a prayer. The faculty members and the attending student ministers and the various denominations were thereby represented, as the faculty personally belonged to three of the contemporary popular churches in that part of the State, at one time including a Quaker. Although two of the before-mentioned teachers were ministers, there was never any attempt to enhance the instruction, because some were ministers, by College.

The design to organize a Y.M.C.A. was never carried out, since, as stated, it is not clear from the limited information at Savoy College reported in Y.M.C.A. Convention Reports, but the Y.M.C.A. was a very popular organization in colleges and schools. A very popular organization at the college at the time of Savoy College, however, was the Band of Hope, a national temperance promotional association.
